notes.sage_chat.gemini: Cloud chat path, the one the student is actively waiting on. The nightly chat harness measures a real p50 of 1283ms and p95 of 1816ms against Gemini. This bar (6000ms) sits well above that baseline so ordinary network/provider jitter never pages anyone, but it is tight enough to catch roughly a 3x regression in the path students feel most directly.
notes.sage_chat.ollama: Local chat path (used when ai_provider="local"). Accepted production behavior is ~20-70s/turn with reasoning disabled by default (see PR #147 in .claude/MEMORY.md); docs/plans/2026-07-02-local-model-acceptance-report.md:48 recorded local latency around 70s and set no target at the time. This bar (90000ms / 90s) sits just above that accepted range so normal local-model turns pass, while a genuine stall or an accidental reasoning-enabled deployment still breaches.
notes.defaultP95Ms: Background/extraction callSites (sage_post.goals/discovery/mood/classroom, sage_auto.briefing, sage_agent.*, sage_embedding_*, sage_memory_*, sage_form_search_*, chat_file_gist). These run off the critical path (fire-and-forget or async), so the bar is looser than cloud chat, but it is not split per provider the way sage_chat is: this is a best-guess default (45000ms / 45s), picked to sit comfortably above typical short-prompt local latency without reaching all the way to the full local chat bar. Revisit once the script's own p95 output accumulates real background-call data — see docs/SLO.md.
notes.modelProviders: LlmCallLog.model records the real model tag (e.g. "gemma4:e4b"), not the provider class. The bars above are keyed by provider, so this maps each known tag to its provider bucket. Resolution is: an entry in perProviderP95Ms[callSite] keyed by the exact model tag wins (use that to give a per-role model its own bar), then this provider bucket, then defaultP95Ms. A tag that matches none of these is reported as "NO SLO BAR" rather than silently checked against the default -- for sage_chat the default is 7.5x too loose for cloud and 2x too tight for local, so a silent fallthrough both hides regressions and invents breaches.
